title: Checking the summary against the code
intro: I kept CodeRabbit’s layer model and focused on one review task in Formbricks #8650: check a summary, inspect the access guard, then get back to the call. The original already has summary jumps, viewed status and Focus.
rows: Six summary points share an 82-line range.
Each point links to a smaller code range. Full wording and the whole function remain available; a highlight is a starting point, not proof.
The access check continues in another file.
Inspect guard opens the workspace and entitlement checks. Return restores the caller’s selection and reading position. This route is manually mapped.
File and display actions sit across several controls.
File actions sit beside the filename; display settings sit above the diff. Less frequent tools move into named menus, which adds a click.
tradeoff_title: Why I kept one code pane
tradeoff: Caller and guard side by side would squeeze both at laptop width. I chose a return action. The comparison uses Unified on both screens: the original fits more code, while M gives files and summary links more room. Focus restores code space.
validation: Layers, J/K, Z and separate seen/viewed states remain. Opening a file marks nothing viewed. Undo reverses Mark viewed. Unified already exists; a compact empty pane in Split is a supporting layout choice.
next: Ask developers to explain the access check on both screens, then find something the summary might miss. Compare missed branches and wrong turns. A precise link can narrow attention too much; the test needs to check that risk.
scope: This prototype covers seven of 52 diffs at commit 23cdac2. Links are manually mapped. The PR is merged; Submit is disabled. Semantic diffs and modified-file review are outside this sample. I have not tested it with developers.
